caseStudies.title: StreetBite - Street food. Zero wait.
caseStudies.description: A Minimalist Real-Time App for Discovering and Pre-Booking Street Food

hero.outcome: A Minimalist Real-Time App for Discovering and Pre-Booking Street Food

overview: StreetBite is a mobile app designed for busy students and office workers to locate real-time street food vendors and pre-book food to avoid queues. This self-initiated UX project explores how to streamline urban street food access through minimal design, real-time data, and step-by-step pickup tracking.
I was responsible for the full UX process — from user research, persona creation, wireframes, UI design, testing, to prototyping.

paragraphs: Many urban users, especially students and professionals, face long queues, unreliable vendor availability, and inconsistent lunch breaks. These issues reduce access to quick, affordable meals during tight schedules.
The main goal was to **minimize friction in street food access** by building a **mobile-first, minimalist app** for discovering nearby vendors and pre-booking food ahead of arrival.

StreetBite simplifies street food discovery through a real-time map, vendor previews, and a 4-step order tracker. By allowing users to pre-book meals and pick them up with a QR code, it eliminates queue frustration.
The design addresses the problem through:
Each feature directly supports the goal of **reducing user effort and waiting time.**
features: A clean map-first home screen with vendor filters
A quick pre-book flow with real-time availability
A minimalist stepper for order tracking (Confirmed → Preparing → Wrapping → Collect)

projectGoals.introduction: The project aimed to solve frustrations faced by busy students and professionals when trying to access street food. Long queues, lack of real-time vendor data, and uncertain wait times made the experience inefficient. StreetBite was designed to offer a minimalist, real-time solution that makes it easy to find vendors and pre-book food before arriving.

goals.title: Streamline vendor discovery with a live map
Enable quick and intuitive food pre-booking
Minimize user wait time through real-time tracking and QR pickup

paragraphs: During the research phase, I conducted short user interviews to better understand the behavior and frustrations of street food buyers—especially university students and busy office workers. These users often rely on quick meals during tight schedules, yet face issues with vendor availability, long queues, and lack of information.
The goal was to uncover pain points with the current street food experience and gather insights to guide a minimalist app that allows real-time discovery and pre-booking of food.
Over 4 days, I interviewed **6 participants remotely** (3 university students, 2 working professionals, and 1 gig worker). Their feedback directly informed StreetBite's UX strategy.
objectives: Understand user frustrations around buying street food during peak hours.
Identify how users currently discover food stalls or make quick food decisions.
Learn what would motivate users to pre-book food ahead of arrival.

findings.title: Lack of Time Leads to Abandonment
findings.description: Busy users often give up on buying food when they see long queues or unpredictable vendor availability. Convenience and speed matter more than food variety.

findings.title: Uncertainty Around Vendor Location & Wait Times
findings.description: Sometimes I go looking for my favorite vendor, but they're not there. Or they say '10 minutes' and it takes 20.

findings.title: Users Want Control Without Complexity
findings.description: I'd love to just tap a few things and know when to pick up. I don't want to talk, call, or guess.

insights.title: 71% of users wanted real-time vendor availability
insights.description: Most participants said they would only use an app if it gave **accurate real-time locations** and **open/close status** of nearby vendors.

insights.title: 60% of users wanted estimated prep + pickup times
insights.description: Time-conscious users expressed interest in **ETA labels** and **prep time indicators** before placing a pre-book order.

insights.title: 45% of users said they'd use the app only if it saved them at least 5 minutes
insights.description: Participants were open to using StreetBite if it meant **less queuing** and a more predictable pickup experience. They wanted something that felt **faster than ordering in person**.

banner.text: Filters helped users discover vendors 40% faster

competitiveResearch.title: Competitive Research
competitiveResearch.description: To assess StreetBite's position in the market, we conducted a competitive analysis of popular food and vendor-related platforms. We evaluated each product based on its ability to offer real-time street vendor visibility, efficient booking, and mobile-first experiences. This helped us uncover key areas where StreetBite could differentiate through speed, simplicity, and vendor trust.

userFlow.title: User Flows
paragraphs: We mapped out key user flows to ensure a frictionless experience from splash screen to food pickup. The primary flow covers user registration via mobile number and OTP verification, then guides users through store discovery via map or list view, food selection, and order placement. Post-order, users can track the status and complete pickup with a QR scan.
These flows helped identify drop-off points, clarify navigation logic, and streamline the checkout experience — ultimately improving usability and speed.

wireframes.title: Wireframes
paragraphs: I created low-fidelity wireframes in Figma based on initial sketches. These helped validate layout ideas early. After feedback from 4 user tests, I iterated on the designs—improving clarity, navigation, and hierarchy. I later enhanced the wireframes with sample images and text for early usability evaluation before moving to high-fidelity prototypes.

uiDesign.title: UI Design
paragraphs: After resolving usability issues, I finalized the UI in Figma. The goal was to create a clean, modern visual identity that reflects the brand's tone—friendly, minimal, and efficient. I drew inspiration from design references and followed platform-specific guidelines to ensure consistency. Final designs were tailored for mobile-first usage, based on user behavior insights gathered during research.

learnings.title: Simplicity drives success
learnings.description: Reducing the flow from 6 to 4 steps decreased drop-offs and improved usability.

learnings.title: Trust is essential
learnings.description: Adding live previews and clear summaries reassured users and reduced hesitation.

learnings.title: Flexibility matters
learnings.description: Entry points like "Start Designing" vs "Instant Quote" catered to different user goals.

learnings.title: Clarity reduces friction
learnings.description: Progress indicators and clean navigation boosted user confidence.

caseStudies.title: Redesigning Wristband Monkey's Online Experience
caseStudies.description: A UX case study to improve the overall user experience and usability of Wristband Monkey's website.

hero.outcome: A UX case study to improve the overall user experience and usability of Wristband Monkey's website.

overview: Wristband Monkey is a leading provider of custom wristbands, serving a diverse customer base including event planners, businesses, students, and organizations. This project aimed to enhance their online experience by addressing usability issues and creating a more modern, intuitive interface.
The redesign focused on improving the overall user experience, streamlining the ordering process, and increasing conversion rates through a user-centered design approach.

paragraphs: The existing Wristband Monkey website suffered from several critical issues that impacted user experience and business performance:
**Outdated UI**: The interface felt dated and didn't reflect modern web design standards, which affected user trust and engagement.
**Poor Usability**: Users struggled to navigate the site, find products, and understand customization options, leading to frustration and abandonment.
**Lack of Mobile Responsiveness**: The website was not optimized for mobile devices, despite a significant portion of users accessing it on smartphones and tablets.
**Complex Ordering Process**: The multi-step ordering process was confusing and had too many friction points, resulting in high cart abandonment rates.
The solution involved a comprehensive user-centered design approach to create a modern, intuitive, and responsive website that addresses all identified pain points.
**User Research**: Conducted extensive user interviews, surveys, and competitor analysis to understand user needs, behaviors, and expectations.
**Streamlined Information Architecture**: Reorganized the site structure based on card sorting exercises and user feedback to make navigation more intuitive.
**Modern UI Design**: Created a fresh, clean interface that builds trust and guides users through the customization and ordering process.
**Mobile-First Approach**: Designed with mobile users in mind, ensuring a seamless experience across all devices.
**Simplified Ordering Flow**: Reduced the ordering process from 6 steps to 4, eliminating unnecessary friction and improving conversion rates.
features: Better visual hierarchy and content organization

projectGoals.introduction: The project aimed to transform Wristband Monkey's online presence through strategic UX improvements.

goals.title: Improve the overall user experience and usability

paragraphs: User research was conducted through multiple methods to gain comprehensive insights into user needs, behaviors, and pain points.
**Methods Used**:
• User interviews with 12 participants across different user segments (event planners, business owners, students, marketing managers)
• Online surveys distributed to 150+ existing and potential customers
• Competitor analysis of 5 leading wristband providers
• Usability testing sessions with 8 participants on the existing website
objectives: Understand user goals and motivations when purchasing wristbands
Identify pain points in the current ordering and customization process
Discover what information users need to make purchasing decisions
Learn about user expectations from similar e-commerce experiences
Understand mobile usage patterns and requirements

findings.title: Navigation Difficulties
findings.description: Users struggled to find specific product types and customization options, leading to frustration and site abandonment.

findings.title: Confusing Ordering Process
findings.description: The multi-step ordering process was unclear, with users unsure about what information was required at each stage.

findings.title: Lack of Clear Information
findings.description: Users wanted more transparent pricing, clearer product descriptions, and better visual representations of customization options.

findings.title: Outdated Design
findings.description: The website's design felt outdated, which affected user trust and perceived credibility of the brand.

findings.title: Cart Abandonment
findings.description: High cart abandonment rates were observed, particularly during the checkout process due to complexity and lack of trust signals.

findings.title: Mobile Experience Issues
findings.description: Users reported significant difficulties using the website on mobile devices, with poor touch targets and unresponsive layouts.

insights.title: Visual-First Approach
insights.description: Users respond better to **visual product showcases** and **interactive customization tools** rather than text-heavy descriptions.

insights.title: Trust Building
insights.description: Clear pricing, **customer reviews**, and **security badges** are essential for building trust and reducing abandonment.

insights.title: Simplification Wins
insights.description: Reducing the ordering process from 6 to 4 steps significantly improved completion rates and user satisfaction.

insights.title: Mobile Priority
insights.description: A significant portion of users access the site on mobile, making **mobile-first design** critical for success.

insights.title: Progressive Disclosure
insights.description: Presenting information in **manageable chunks** and using **progressive disclosure** helps users feel less overwhelmed.

insights.title: Clear Call-to-Actions
insights.description: Prominent, clear CTAs guide users through the journey and reduce decision paralysis.

competitiveResearch.title: Competitive Research
competitiveResearch.description: A comprehensive analysis of leading wristband providers revealed key opportunities for differentiation and improvement. The research compared website design, customization options, pricing transparency, mobile responsiveness, customer support, shipping options, bulk ordering capabilities, and design tools.

userFlow.title: User Flows
paragraphs: User flows were created to map out the optimal paths users should take to complete key tasks, such as finding a product, customizing a wristband, and completing a purchase.

These flows helped identify unnecessary steps, clarify navigation paths, and ensure users can accomplish their goals efficiently. The flows were iterated based on user testing feedback to minimize friction and improve task completion rates.

wireframes.title: Wireframes
paragraphs: Low-fidelity wireframes were created to establish the layout, information hierarchy, and user flow before moving to high-fidelity design. These wireframes focused on functionality and usability rather than visual aesthetics.

Key pages wireframed included the homepage, product listing, product detail, customization interface, cart, checkout, and order confirmation. The wireframes were tested with users to validate the information architecture and identify any usability issues early in the process.

uiDesign.title: UI Design
paragraphs: The UI design phase transformed the wireframes into a modern, visually appealing interface that maintains usability while enhancing the brand experience. The design system includes a cohesive color palette, typography, spacing, and component library.

Key design principles applied include visual hierarchy, clear call-to-actions, consistent navigation, and responsive layouts. The final design was tested with users to ensure it meets both aesthetic and functional requirements.

Usability testing was conducted with 8 participants to validate the new design and identify any remaining usability issues. The testing focused on key user tasks including finding products, customizing wristbands, and completing a purchase.
The testing revealed that the new design was significantly more intuitive and user-friendly compared to the original website.

summary: The redesign of Wristband Monkey's online experience successfully addressed the key usability issues identified in the research phase. Through a user-centered design approach, we created a modern, intuitive, and responsive website that significantly improved the user experience.
The new design streamlined the ordering process, improved navigation, and enhanced mobile responsiveness, resulting in measurable improvements in conversion rates and user satisfaction.
